rows.en:
(Pinon-chan asked me to help her with something,
but what could it be?)

You got here before me? So you can do it
when you try. I'm counting on you today.

I don't mind helping, but...
what exactly do you need help with?

Oh, didn't I tell you what it was about?
The truth is, I want you to help me train
with tongue twisters.
Tongue-twister training?

Indeed. A good operator needs clear diction
so that orders get across.

So I want to practice tongue twisters
for that, but...
I don't really know many tongue twisters.
So I thought I'd have you give me some to try.

I see.
Okay, got it.
Then let's start the training right away.
Okay, I'll start with an easy one.
Right! Bring it on!

Say the title of Sheryl's fourth single,
"What 'bout my star?",
three times in a row.
Go!

What 'bout my star!
What 'bout my star!
What 'bout my st-nyaaa~!!
rows.notes: The Japanese garbles the last 'star' (sutaa) into 'su-nyaa'; rendered 'st-nyaaa~'.

rows.en: Yes! Perfect!
...Um, at the end you said 'st-nyaaa~'...

I didn't flub it!
You just weren't listening properly!
Huh... W-was that how it went...?

Honestly... You're hopeless.
Then give me a harder tongue twister.

Okay, next is:
"Gubaba hop-hop, three hop-hops,
add 'em up, hop-hop, six hop-hops."
rows.notes: Parody of the classic Japanese twister 'kaeru pyoko pyoko mi pyoko pyoko, awasete pyoko pyoko mu pyoko pyoko' with Gubaba in place of the frog; translated literally so Pinon's flub on the first word (c12006) still works.

rows.en: Got it. Here I go!

rows.notes: Pinon flubs the very first word, Gubaba, after a long pause (Japanese 'gubyabya').

rows.en: (Huh?! She flubs it THERE?!)
...I flubbed it.
(And now she's crying!)

P-Pinon-chan!
I'll treat you to ice cream! See? Hippo-cow!

(Then again, there's no way she'd stop crying
over something like that...)
Huh?! Really?!
(Sh-she stopped crying?!)

Then it's decided! Let's hurry to Folmo!
Come on, come on!
Don't rush so much, Pinon-chan.

(In the end, it didn't turn into tongue-twister
training at all... Is that okay...?)

(Well, Pinon-chan ended up happy,
so I guess this works too.)

(Pinon-chan asked me to help her with something,
but what could it be?)

I see.
Okay, got it.
Then let's start the training right away.

(Then again, there's no way she'd stop crying
over something like that...)

(In the end, it didn't turn into tongue-twister
training at all... Is that okay...?)

(Well, Pinon-chan ended up happy,
so I guess this works too.)

(I'm helping Pinon-chan with her tongue-twister
training again today, but...)

(No matter how many times she practices,
she flubs it in the same spot...)
Th-that one was perfect, right?!
No, you flubbed it...

That can't be!
You misheard!
(Even though she flubbed it that obviously...)

...Pinon-chan,
you've practiced hard enough today. Why don't
we go to Folmo and get some soft serve?

Hey, \p...
You're not trying to change the subject, are you?

Y-you're imagining things.
Come on, let's hurry.

(Well, an operator who flubs her lines now and then
like Pinon-chan isn't so bad...
Probably......)

(No matter how many times she practices,
she flubs it in the same spot...)
No, you flubbed it...

...Pinon-chan,
you've practiced hard enough today. Why don't
we go to Folmo and get some soft serve?

Y-you're imagining things.
Come on, let's hurry.

(Well, an operator who flubs her lines now and then
like Pinon-chan isn't so bad...
Probably......)

(Pinon-chan asked me to help her with something
again, but what could it be?)

(I bet it's helping her with some kind
of training again today.)

\p.
Sorry I kept you waiting.

Hey, Pinon-chan.
I just got here myself.

I see. Then there's no problem.
Let's go, then.

Umm... Go where?
You haven't told me what I'm helping with
this time either...
Hm, now that you mention it, I haven't...
W-well, um, today...
I want you to help me with swimming practice.

Swimming?
So does that mean, Pinon-chan, you...
S-so what if it does?! I can't swim!!
(I can't believe Pinon-chan can't swim...)
(No, actually, it's just what I expected...)
S-sorry I kept you waiting.

Okay then, swimming practice...
Huh? Pinon-chan,
are you okay without your glasses?

Well, I can't exactly wear glasses in the pool.
And you're here, so I'll probably be fine.
Hm? \p... It is you, right?
...Are you really okay?

I-I'm fine!
It was just a little hard to see, that's all!

But you can't tell who I am unless you get
this close, right? I knew it...

You're worrying way too much!
Hmm?! Are you treating me like a child?
That's not what I mean...

If I say I'm fine, then I'm fine!
Honestly...
Ah! Watch out, Pinon-chan!
Huh? Hyaah!!

uncertain: c11995: Sheryl's single title written in full-width letters in the source, rendered as plain ASCII "What 'bout my star?" (not in the glossary songs list).
c11997/c12000: Pinon's flub on the last 'star' (su-nyaa) rendered 'st-nyaaa~'.

c12004/c12006: Gubaba version of the frog tongue twister translated literally ('Gubaba hop-hop, three hop-hops...') so that the flub 'Gubyabya!' on the first word still lands; not an English tongue twister.
kamu (to flub / trip over one's words) rendered 'flub' throughout.
missing_glossary: What 'bout my star? (Sheryl's fourth single, per c11995)
